final_response:
Ghostty loading on the desktop side is solid. I have everything needed.

VERDICT: **REVISE**
CONFIDENCE: **HIGH**

SUMMARY: Items 1, 4, 5, and 6 are genuinely resolved and correctly implemented in `RemoteTerminal.tsx`. However, item 2 is only half-done (the server route exists, but `getTerminalPreferences()` never calls it — the browser silently gets a hardcoded fallback), item 3 is not done at all (`DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` is exported and consumed by zero call sites), and I found an unrelated hard blocker: browser pairing is broken by a serde casing mismatch, so no browser client can reach the terminal at all.

## FINDINGS

**[evidence] [functional] [BLOCKING] Browser pairing is broken — serde field casing mismatch.**
`ui/src/remote/PairingPage.tsx:25` and `ui/src/remote/RemoteApp.tsx:23` both POST `{ code, deviceName }`, but `PairExchangeRequest` at `src-tauri/src/remote/server.rs:33-37` lacks `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and therefore expects `device_name`. Every other struct in `src-tauri/src/remote/protocol.rs` (lines 5, 15, 22, 31, 39, 62) carries that attribute — this one is the outlier. Axum rejects the body with 422 before the handler runs, so `/api/v1/pair/exchange` fails 100% of the time from a browser. This makes the entire Remote Web surface unreachable, which supersedes any parity question.
Fix: add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` to `PairExchangeRequest`.

**[evidence] [functional] [BLOCKING] Item 2 is only half-resolved: the preferences endpoint has no consumer.**
`src-tauri/src/remote/server.rs:406-411` exposes `GET /api/v1/terminal/preferences` and it is routed at line 425 — that half is correct. But `getTerminalPreferences()` in `ui/src/lib/tauri.ts:89-125` branches on `!isTauri()` and returns a **hardcoded inline object literal**, never issuing a fetch. `RemoteTerminal.tsx` → `useTerminalSettings()` → `fetchCachedNativePreferences()` → `getTerminalPreferences()` therefore resolves to `source: "defaults"` in the browser regardless of the user's actual Ghostty config. The route is dead code. Remote Web silently renders with different font, size, cursor style, and full ANSI theme than Desktop — the exact parity failure this item was meant to close.
Fix: in the `!isTauri()` branch, `await defaultRemoteClient.fetchJson<TerminalPreferences>("/api/v1/terminal/preferences")` (the `RemoteClient` at `ui/src/lib/remoteClient.ts:36` already attaches the bearer token), falling back to the literal only on failure.

**[evidence] [design-system] [BLOCKING] Item 3 is unresolved: `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` has zero consumers.**
It is declared at `ui/src/lib/tauri.ts:1` and, per a workspace-wide grep, referenced in no other file. The three places that actually decide a font all hardcode bare `"monospace"`: `tauri.ts:92` (browser fallback), `terminalSettings.ts:66` (`FALLBACK_PREFERENCES`), and `terminalSettings.ts:132` (`resolveTerminalSettings` final coalesce). Both surfaces fall back to the OS default monospace, not the Orca stack.
Secondary problem: the stack's first entry is `"Geist Mono"`, and no such face is bundled — `ui/src/index.css:1-4` registers only `geist-variable.woff2` as the **sans** family `"Geist"`, and `ui/src/assets/` contains no mono file. Applying the constant as-is would fall through to `JetBrains Mono`/`MesloLGS NF` if installed locally and otherwise land back on `monospace`, which is non-deterministic across Desktop and Remote and reintroduces the parity gap under a different name.
Fix: substitute `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` at all three sites, and either bundle a Geist Mono `@font-face` or drop the unshipped first entry so the stack resolves identically on both surfaces.

**[evidence] [design-system] [MAJOR] Remote surface bypasses the token layer wholesale.**
`ui/DESIGN.md:3-5` states the contract verbatim: "no color, size, spacing, or motion value may appear in a component unless it traces back to a token named here," and §1 adds "Components reference the **Tailwind semantic name**, never a hex value." `RemoteTerminal.tsx` uses raw hex throughout its chrome (`bg-[#0a0a0a]`, `bg-[#12141a]`, `border-[#262833]`, `text-[#d4d4d4]`, `text-[#c9d1d9]`, `bg-[#1a1d26]`, `text-[#8b949e]`), as does `MobileKeyDock.tsx` (`bg-[#12141a]`, `border-[#2c3140]`, `bg-[#1e222d]`, plus `bg-blue-600`/`text-red-400` from Tailwind's default palette, which is not the token palette). `PairingPage.tsx` uses the `neutral-*`/`red-*` default ramps. Compare `TerminalPane.tsx:196-201`, which correctly uses `bg-terminal`, `border-destructive/30`, `text-destructive`.
Only `#0a0a0a` even coincides with a token (`--terminal`, `index.css:91`); the rest are invented values with no token backing — `#12141a` and `#262833` do not correspond to `--card` `#171717` or `--border`. Desktop and Remote are visibly different products under the same brand.
Fix: replace with `bg-terminal`, `bg-card`, `border-border`, `text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground`, and the `--status-*` utilities. Note `MobileKeyDock.tsx:135` already reaches for `text-foreground`, so the token utilities are in scope and available.

**[evidence] [functional] [MINOR] Latched Ctrl silently swallows non-alphabetic keys.**
`MobileKeyDock.tsx:38-41` composes `ctrl-${action}` for any action, so latching Ctrl then tapping an arrow yields `ctrl-up`. In `RemoteTerminal.tsx:sendKey`, the `key.startsWith("ctrl-")` branch requires `char.length === 1`; `"up"` fails that guard and nothing is sent — no keystroke, no feedback, and the latch has already been cleared. Same for `ctrl-pageup`, `ctrl-home`, etc. `RemoteUI.test.tsx:56-57` asserts `ctrl-tab` is dispatched from the dock but never asserts what reaches the wire, so the gap is untested.
Fix: either encode modified special keys as proper CSI sequences (`\x1b[1;5A` for Ctrl+Up) or have the dock refuse to latch onto keys it cannot encode.

## WHAT IS GOOD (must not regress)

- **Item 1 — mount branch.** `main.tsx:7,11` correctly gates on `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` and mounts `<RemoteApp />` in the browser; the service-worker registration is correctly gated to non-Tauri too.
- **Item 4 — viewport resize.** `RemoteTerminal.tsx:135-165` is well built: a single rAF handle with `cancelAnimationFrame` before rescheduling gives true coalescing, `visualViewport.height` drives `rootRef` inline height (correct for the iOS keyboard case), and every `fit()` is guarded by `clientWidth > 0`, avoiding the classic zero-dimension NaN crash. The listener is registered on both `window` and `visualViewport` and removed on both.
- **Item 5 — lifecycle.** The `onData` disposable is captured into `onDataDisposable` in the async `.then()` and disposed in cleanup, alongside `abortController.abort()`, WS close, WebGL cleanup, and `terminal.dispose()`. The `isDisposed` flag is re-checked after both awaits, so a fast unmount during async load disposes correctly instead of leaking a terminal.
- **Item 6 — alt encoding.** `RemoteTerminal.tsx:227-229` correctly emits `\x1b` + char for `alt-*`, and critically it is ordered **before** the `ctrl-` branch, so no shadowing. Ctrl maps via `charCodeAt - 64` with a proper `1..=26` range check; `ctrl-c` correctly routes to the server-side `signal` control message rather than a raw byte.
- **Wire protocol.** The client's JSON `{type:"resize"|"signal"}` messages match `ClientControlMessage` (`protocol.rs:46-51`) exactly, and the server enforces `can_control` on both input writes and interrupts (`server.rs:340-356`).
- **Desktop `TerminalPane.tsx`** remains the correct reference: `ResizeObserver`-driven, all disposables released, font-ready await before construction, and token-based styling.
- Typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) is clean, `cargo check` is clean, and all 226 tests across 38 files pass in a single run.

## BLOCKING

1. Add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` to `PairExchangeRequest` (`src-tauri/src/remote/server.rs:33`) — browser pairing is completely broken without it.
2. Make `getTerminalPreferences()` fetch `/api/v1/terminal/preferences` in the browser branch (`ui/src/lib/tauri.ts:89`) — item 2 is not actually wired.
3. Apply `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` at `tauri.ts:92`, `terminalSettings.ts:66`, and `terminalSettings.ts:132`, and resolve the missing Geist Mono face — item 3 is not implemented.
4. Convert `RemoteTerminal.tsx`, `MobileKeyDock.tsx`, and `PairingPage.tsx` to token utilities per `ui/DESIGN.md` — required for the stated design-system parity goal.
